rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices. Coordinators, including software providers, may not use such software or an algorithmic device to facilitate agreements or parallel pricing coordination among competing residential landlords. Spreadsheets that need human analysis and operate without AI are not covered. Neither are databases that only query unprocessed data, or government entities setting rents through affordability controls.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental property owners and to coordinators operating algorithmic revenue management software or algorithmic devices that use nonpublic, competitively sensitive information from multiple owners.
coverage.other_conditions: Excluded from the 'coordinating function' definition: research, statistical or testing use not used in setting rents; public rent estimates available at no cost; equal-terms real estate brokerage databases that do not set or recommend rents; government affordability-control programs.

rules.exemptions: Spreadsheets operating without AI that require human analysis; databases that only use an algorithm to query unprocessed data; government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls; certain research, public-estimate and brokerage-database uses.
rules.effective_date_note: The passages state the signing date (July 20) but no effective date.
citation_aliases: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent Act
rules.quoted_span: The FAIR Act prohibits residential rental property owners from using algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices.
rules.review_note: The passages do not give the effective date, so status 'in_force' is assumed from the July 20, 2026 signing. Penalties and enforcement are not shown in the passages. The bill text (D069) is partial and may be an earlier version; the definitions follow the amended text.
rules.source_notes: Enactment date and summary come from a secondary law-firm alert (DX16). Definitions come from the official bill text (D069).
